messages:
maya: FYI from tonight's nova-ensemble canary: streaming funcall plumbing produced a new failure mode where partial-array emissions cause the streaming parser to accept invalid JSON (trailing-comma) and downstream schema validator rejects it. fp16 baseline had 0.5% parse->schema failures; nova-int8 ensemble observed 2.6%.
maya: quick reproduction: model streams an array of actions incrementally, but some chunks end with a dangling comma because the emitter flushes mid-array. parser that tries to be "helpful" reconstructs frames into a single string but doesn't normalize trailing commas. result: JSON parses in lenient parser but fails strict schema check.
kevin: can you paste captured frames?
maya: raw frames (>> marks separate frames):
```
>> {"actions": [
>> {"type":"add_tag","tag":"urgent"},
>> {"type":"assign","user":"ops"},
>> 
>> {"type":"notify","channel":"#alerts"}
>> ]}
```
maya: note frame3 contains just "\n" (empty) which the concat logic left as a dangling comma at the end of frame2 in some cases. strict JSON validator complains about trailing comma.
nora: why does lenient parser succeed sometimes? are client libs enabling JS-style trailing-comma tolerance?
kevin: yep older node parsers sometimes allow it or apps call eval-like routines. our schema checks use strict JSON Schema validators so they reject. the inconsistency leads to only some customers seeing errors.
ops-bot: Canary alert: nova-ensemble-int8 stream_schema_fail_rate=2.6% (+2.1% vs baseline)
maya: initial mitigations tested locally: 1) server-side NDJSON envelope per action (emit each action as self-contained line), 2) postprocess strip-trailing-commas before validation, 3) client-side buffer-until-array-close heuristics (wait for matching brackets before parse).
kevin: NDJSON per-action seems safest short-term: makes each frame independently parseable and avoids array-fragment edgecases. downside: changes contract (now multiple messages instead of single actions array). but we can keep adapter that folds lines back to array for downstream consumers.
nora: strip-trailing-commas is cheap but risky; we might accidentally join unrelated frames. need robust trimming logic: remove comma if followed by whitespace+closing bracket within small lookahead.
maya: tried NDJSON shim in canary with small batch (1k): stream_schema_fail drops to 0.4% for int8. also added conservative client buffer fallback: if parser fails on frame, hold one more frame and retry join. that eliminated ~40% of residuals in replay.
kevin: agree on two-track: (A) push NDJSON shim as canary flag use_stream_ndjson=true, (B) add parser safe-join fallback in SDK for streaming parse errors. open kernel ticket for flush policy since int8 chunk sizes are higher variance.
nora: small additional safety: attach X-stream-frag-id per-frame so we can dedupe/trace fragmented payloads end-to-end. helps debugging and repair heuristics.
ops-bot: Canary run scheduled: 8k samples with use_stream_ndjson starting 1767780000 UTC.
canary-bot: Canary started by maya.
maya: action items: (1) push NDJSON shim to canary, (2) roll parser fallback to SDK, (3) nora to add frame-level tracing header, (4) kevin to open kernel ticket with int8 token-flush histogram. I'll upload three failing raw traces to the ticket. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
